newsitem.title: USA: Tanker admits to pumping polluted water into sea.
newsitem.headline: Tanker admits to pumping polluted water into sea.

text.p: A Texas shipping company has admitted to illegally pumping oily bilge water into the Atlantic Ocean in 1993 in the first U.S. prosecution of its type, a U.S. attorney announced Tuesday.

"Environmental crime is one of our top white collar crimes," said U.S. Attorney Charles Wilson in Tampa. "We have been working aggressively to prosecute these cases and make sure these polluters obey the law and clean up their act."
The company admitted to violating the Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships.

On March 30, 1993, the captain of the 678-foot (207 metre) tanker M/V Frances Hammer ordered the illegal dumping, which was carried out by the chief mate. A steward videotaped the incident and eventually turned the three-minute tape over to authorities.
The ship was built in the early 1980s by Occidental Petroleum Corp. to carry phosphoric acid to Russia, returning to the United States with liquid anhydrous ammonia.
Coast Guard officials did not know if the ship was still owned by Occidental but the charges were filed against a Texas-based company, Ocean Chemical Carriers Inc.
OCCI and the ship officers have pleaded guilty.

Under plea bargaining agreements, still to be approved by a court, the company faces $250,000 in fines and restitution and must publish a public apology in a Tampa newspaper and a maritime trade journal.

The captain, Peter Thorpe, faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and suspension of his license for two years. Chief mate James Gerhard faces $5,000 and loss of his license for one year.
